entities.summary:
Barisone II of Torres was the giudice of the Judicate of Logudoro from 1153 to 1186. He was the son and successor of Gonario II, who abdicated the throne and retired to the monastery of Clairvaux to live out his days. Barisone II played a significant role in the regional politics of Sardinia during the 12th century. His tenure was marked by a series of power struggles with neighboring nobles and the influence of the Holy Roman Empire.

He also oversaw the development of the Judicate of Logudoro's administrative structures, including the creation of a new tax system and the establishment of trade relations with neighboring cities. Barisone II's legacy extends to the modern-day Republic of Sardinia, where his descendants continued to play important roles in regional politics.

Despite his significant contributions, Barisone II's life remains somewhat of a mystery, with many details lost to the passage of time. Nevertheless, his impact on the history of Sardinia and the surrounding region cannot be overstated.

The decline of the Judicate of Logudoro during Barisone II's reign is often attributed to the decline of the Pisan Empire and the subsequent rise of the Republic of Pisa, which would eventually supplant the Judicate as the dominant power in Sardinia.

Barisone II's story serves as a reminder of the complex and often brutal nature of medieval politics, where the line between loyalty and betrayal was frequently blurred.
